root.name: Queen's Gambit Declined: Traditional Variation
root.moves: 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 e6 3. Nf3 d5 4. Bg5

overview: White pins the f6 knight at once with 4.Bg5 and Black plays the usual 4...Be7, then ...O-O and ...Nbd7 with the Orthodox set-up (or ...dxc4 and ...h6 ideas). White usually builds with e3, Nc3, Qc2 or Rc1 and may choose between exchanging on d5 and the Capablanca freeing manoeuvre. Play is positional, with Black solid but slightly cramped.

white_ideas.idea: Pin the knight, then e3, Nc3, Bd3 and cxd5 with a minority attack.
Keep the tension and use the space advantage on the queenside.

black_ideas.idea: Develop ...Be7, ...O-O and ...Nbd7 and free with ...c5 or ...dxc4.
Use the Lasker simplification (...Ne4) or Tartakower (...b6, ...Bb7) to equalise.

typical_structures.structure: QGD with pawns c4/d4/e3 against ...d5/...e6, tension on d5.

character.notes: Orthodox QGD: very hard to break down, few ways to lose quickly.

level.notes: Orthodox QGD anchor is Intermediate: plans plain, memory modest.
